newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA asks Nobel laureate to broker talks with Spain.
newsitem.headline: ETA asks Nobel laureate to broker talks with Spain.

text.p: Argentine Nobel peace laureate Adolfo Perez Esquivel has been asked by Basque separatist rebels to mediate peace talks with the Spanish government, and has written to Spanish premier Jose Maria Aznar.

In an interview with Spain's Europa Press agency published late Monday night, Perez Esquivel said he had met representatives of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) a month ago in Buenos Aires to discuss possible mediation efforts.

"What I can do is try to bring the two sides together, but if the Spanish government is not willing, our intervention will not have much sense," said Perez Esquivel, who won the Nobel prize for his 1970s human-rights work in Argentina.
ETA used Perez Esquivel as a go-between to start talks with the Socialist government last year. However, the initiative died as Spain's general election in March approached.
The new conservative government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar has ruled out talks with ETA unless it renounces violence.
After the meeting with ETA, Perez Esquivel said he had sent a letter to Aznar.
"We are still waiting to see what the reply will be. Until now there has been no reaction," he said.
The possibility of talks became more remote after ETA ran a bombing campaign in tourist resorts last summer and kidnapped two people they are still holding.

ETA has killled some 800 people since 1968 in its drive for an independent Basque state. The Interior Ministry estimates ETA street violence this year alone has cost the government about 800 million pesetas ($6 million).
